claims: The IRS failure-to-file penalty is typically 5% of the unpaid taxes for each month or part of a month a tax return is late.
The IRS failure-to-file penalty is capped at 25% of the unpaid tax.
The failure-to-pay penalty is 0.5% per month.
If you also fail to pay on time, the failure-to-file penalty is reduced by the failure-to-pay penalty.
The total penalty for failure-to-file and failure-to-pay combined is 5% per month.
For returns filed more than 60 days late in 2026, the minimum penalty is the lesser of $525 or 100% of the tax owed.
If you are owed a refund, there is no penalty for filing late.
The IRS charges interest on unpaid taxes, currently around 7% annually, adjusted quarterly.
Penalties may be waived if you can show "reasonable cause" for the delay (e.g., natural disaster, serious illness).
The deadline to file a return or extension is April 15.
